dataset_metadata.disclaimer: New AI-generated English drafts of the recorded Classical Chinese; not scholarly reviewed. Original source interpretations are not verified geometry or modern etymology.

shuowen:5001.text: To carry a load. Formed from 人, with 可 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5002.text: To carry a load. Formed from 人, with 詹 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5003.text: To set out or provide. Formed from 人, with 共 indicating the sound. Another explanation: to supply.

shuowen:5004.text: To wait or hold ready. Formed from 人 and 待.

shuowen:5005.text: To hold in reserve. Formed from 人, with 諸 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5006.text: Careful or prepared. Formed from 人, with 𤰈 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5007.text: Ranks arranged to the left and right in the central courtyard are called 位. Formed from 人 and 立.

shuowen:5008.text: To guide. Formed from 人, with 賓 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5009.text: Part of the name 偓佺. Formed from 人, with 屋 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5010.text: 偓佺, an immortal. Formed from 人, with 全 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5011.text: To submit in one’s heart. Formed from 人, with 聶 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5012.text: To bind or constrain. Formed from 人, with 勺 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5013.text: Those of equal rank or generation. Formed from 人, with 齊 indicating the sound. The Spring and Autumn Commentary says: “We petty people.”

shuowen:5014.text: A class or generation. Formed from 人, with 侖 indicating the sound. Another explanation: the way.

shuowen:5015.text: Equal. Formed from 人, with 牟 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5016.text: Strong. Formed from 人, with 皆 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “Stalwart officers.” Another explanation: together.

shuowen:5017.text: Together. Formed from 人, with 具 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5018.text: To gather. Formed from 人, with 贊 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5019.text: To join side by side. Formed from 人, with 并 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5020.text: To assist. Formed from 人, with 尃 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5021.text: Apprehensive. Formed from 人, with 式 indicating the sound. The Spring and Autumn Discourses of the States says: “In his heart he is apprehensive.”

shuowen:5022.text: To assist. Formed from 人, with 甫 indicating the sound. Read like 撫.

shuowen:5023.text: To lean upon. Formed from 人, with 奇 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5024.text: To lean upon. Formed from 人, with 衣 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5025.text: To follow or continue. Formed from 人, with 乃 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5026.text: Convenient or well fitted. Formed from 人, with 次 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “Thumb ring and arm guard are well fitted.” Another explanation: in succession.

shuowen:5027.text: To follow or assist, 佽. Formed from 人, with 耳 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5028.text: Convenient or helpful, 佽. Formed from 人, with 疌 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5029.text: To attend upon. Formed from 人, with 寺 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5030.text: To lean. Formed from 人 and 頃; 頃 also indicates the sound.

shuowen:5031.text: The side. Formed from 人, with 則 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5032.text: At ease. Formed from 人, with 安 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5033.text: Quiet. Formed from 人, with 血 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “The secluded temple is quiet.”

shuowen:5034.text: To give. Formed from 寸 holding something before a person.

shuowen:5035.text: To employ or send. Formed from 人, with 甹 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5036.text: To employ or send, 俜. Formed from 人, with 夾 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5037.text: 儃何, perhaps a leisurely or lingering manner; the gloss is uncertain. Formed from 人, with 亶 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5038.text: A manner of walking. Formed from 人, with 先 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5039.text: To raise. Formed from 人 and 卬.

shuowen:5040.text: To stand. Formed from 人, with 豆 indicating the sound. Read like 樹.

shuowen:5041.text: A drooping appearance. Formed from 人, with 纍 indicating the sound. Another explanation: lazy and slack.

shuowen:5042.text: At ease. Formed from 人, with 坐 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5043.text: To raise or extol. Formed from 人, with 爯 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5044.text: To group together in threes and fives. Formed from 人 and 五.

shuowen:5045.text: To organize into tens for mutual protection. Formed from 人 and 十.

shuowen:5046.text: To organize together in tens and hundreds. Formed from 人 and 百.

shuowen:5047.text: To meet. Formed from 人, with 𠯑 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “When shall we meet?” Another explanation: 𠈲𠈲, a forceful appearance.

shuowen:5048.text: To join. Formed from 人, with 合 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5049.text: Subtle. Formed from 人 and 攴, with abbreviated 豈 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5050.text: Crafty. Formed from 人, with 原 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5051.text: To rise. Formed from 人 and 乍.

shuowen:5052.text: Not genuine. Formed from 人, with 叚 indicating the sound. Another explanation: to reach. The Book of Yu says: “Reaching those above and below.”

shuowen:5053.text: To borrow. Formed from 人, with 昔 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5054.text: To advance gradually. Formed from 人 and 又 holding 帚, like the advance of sweeping; 又 means hand.

shuowen:5055.text: To sell. Formed from 人, with 𧷏 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5056.text: To watch and look out. Formed from 人, with 矦 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5057.text: To return or repay. Formed from 人, with 賞 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5058.text: Talent and ability. Formed from 人, with 堇 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5059.text: To replace. Formed from 人, with 弋 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5060.text: A measure or standard. Formed from 人, with 義 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5061.text: Near. Formed from 人, with 㫄 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5062.text: To resemble. Formed from 人, with 㠯 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5063.text: At ease. When something is inconvenient for a person, change it. Formed from 人 and 更.

shuowen:5064.text: To tally or match. Formed from 人, with 壬 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5065.text: To explain by comparison. Another explanation: to glimpse through a gap. Formed from 人 and 見. The Odes says: “As though she were Heaven’s younger sister.”

shuowen:5066.text: Abundant. Formed from 人, with 憂 indicating the sound. Another explanation: a performer.

shuowen:5067.text: Joyful. Formed from 人, with 喜 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5068.text: Rich. Formed from 人, with 春 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5069.text: Whole. The Lost Book of Zhou says: “I truly lack understanding, thereby 俒 my elder uncle,” perhaps “keeping him whole”; the quotation is uncertain. Formed from 人 and 完.

shuowen:5070.text: Restrained or economical. Formed from 人, with 僉 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5071.text: To face toward. Formed from 人, with 面 indicating the sound. The Minor Rules of Propriety says: “One presenting a wine jar turns its spout toward himself.”

shuowen:5072.text: Custom or habitual practice. Formed from 人, with 谷 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5073.text: To increase. Formed from 人, with 卑 indicating the sound. Another explanation: 俾 is a doorkeeper.

shuowen:5074.text: To assist or increase, 俾. Formed from 人, with 兒 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5075.text: At peace. Formed from 人, with 𢡃 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5076.text: To direct or employ, glossed 伶; the recorded gloss is uncertain. Formed from 人, with 吏 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5077.text: To look both left and right. Formed from 人, with 癸 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5078.text: To perform or play. Formed from 人, with 令 indicating the sound. Yizhou has Jianling County, 建伶.

shuowen:5079.text: Flowing in graceful succession, 棽儷. Formed from 人, with 麗 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5080.text: A relay or express conveyance. Formed from 人, with 專 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5081.text: A minor attendant. Formed from 人 and 官. The Odes says: “Command that attendant.”

shuowen:5082.text: Good. Formed from 人, with 介 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “Good men are the defenses.”

shuowen:5083.text: To be capable. Formed from 人, with 子 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5084.text: To escort. Formed from 人, with 灷 indicating the sound. Lü Buwei says: “The Youshen clan sent Yi Yin as escort with their daughter.” Ancient writing uses it for 訓.

shuowen:5085.text: Slow or gentle. Formed from 人, with 余 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5086.text: Secluded and poor. Formed from 人, with 屏 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5087.text: Bending and stretching. Formed from 人, with 申 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5088.text: Clumsy. Formed from 人, with 且 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5089.text: Weak or brittle in resolve. Formed from 人, with 然 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5090.text: Weak. Formed from 人 and 耎.

shuowen:5091.text: To turn away or oppose. Formed from 人, with 咅 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5092.text: To draw out or raise the price. Formed from 人, with 焉 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5093.text: False or assumed. Formed from 人, with 朁 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5094.text: To presume or falsely assume. Another explanation: to doubt one another. Formed from 人 and 疑.

shuowen:5095.text: Inclined or partial. Formed from 人, with 扁 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5096.text: Wild or mad. Formed from 人, with 長 indicating the sound. Another explanation: a group of ten, 什.

shuowen:5097.text: Confused. Formed from 人, with 薨 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5098.text: To cover or obscure. Formed from 人, with 壽 indicating the sound.

shuowen:5099.text: To obstruct and conceal. Formed from 人, with 舟 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “Who deceives my beloved?”

shuowen:5100.text: Shallow. Formed from 人, with 戔 indicating the sound.
